chapters.html:
Prologue: The Watch

  1. Weather, March 9, 1961: NOAA GHCN-Daily, T. F. Green Airport, Warwick, R.I. (USW00014765), the station nearest Providence. Daily values: maximum 42°F, minimum 31°F, precipitation 1.08 in for the observation day, with 0.3 in of snowfall; weather types fog, sleet, glaze, rain and snow. The peak gust, 33.3 mph from the southeast, is a single observation timed at 4:12 a.m., not a sustained or all-day figure. These are readings at Warwick, not in the city of Providence.
  2. Yuri Gagarin's orbital flight, April 12, 1961, thirty-four days after Laurence's death.
  3. Fox Point hurricane barrier: authorized under the Flood Control Act of 1958. Published Army Corps and secondary accounts give different years (1960 or 1961) for the start of construction.
  4. Death at St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, March 9, 1961, aged 53, after a brief illness; home 644 River Avenue; born in Edinburgh; parents given as the late Robert and Elizabeth (Anderson) Douglas; fifteen years dressing windows for Pawtucket firms; survivors: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). Elizabeth Douglas was born Elizabeth Millar McDonald; "Anderson" is the surname the obituary gives (see Chapter 5).
  5. Lung cancer, and the family's not knowing of it until his hospitalization: recollection of the author's mother.
  6. Providence city directories 1960 (p. 287): displayman, Carter's Men Store, Pawtucket; 1961 (p. 259): window displays, 644 River Avenue; Constance E., nurse, Roger Williams General Hospital.
  7. Birth as Lawrence Brown; mother Agnes Brown, domestic servant; father's particulars blank: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image).
  8. Name as Laurence Brown Douglas: naturalization petition 139903, Western District of Pennsylvania; oath of allegiance and admission to citizenship May 6, 1943.

Chapter 1: The Ploughmen

  1. William Brown, ploughman, and Agnes Brown, maiden surname McGarth, as George Brown's parents: death register of George Brown, Edston, April 5, 1886 (original image).
  2. McGarth household, Tweedsmuir, 1851: Scotland census (index entries and other researchers' family-tree profiles; original page not seen). Jane McGarth's birthplace is the Dumfriesshire parish of Wamphray.
  3. Children of William Brown and Agnes McGarth: 1871 and 1881 Scotland censuses (index entries) and family-tree profiles compiled by other researchers.
  4. Lawrence Tweedie Brown, b. September 14, 1860, Peebles, parents William Brown and Agnes McGarth: Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, Ancestry 60143/8630065 (index). Same household as George, 1871 census, Ancestry 1104/3369754 (index).
  5. George Brown, b. July 18, 1862, Peebles: family tree compiled by another researcher; consistent with his age (23) at death in 1886.
  6. Isabella Graham, b. about 1864, Cambusnethan; Lawrence Tweedie Brown's residences and death in 1943: censuses (index) and family trees; Quebec burial record of a son naming both parents.
  7. The family's understanding that Agnes McGarth Brown named her son for her uncle Lawrence: family knowledge, stated by the author.

Chapter 2: Agnes

  1. Marriage of George Brown and Christina Henderson, June 1, 1883, Quothquan, Libberton: stated in both daughters' birth entries (original images).
  2. Christina Henderson, b. March 19, 1860, Libberton; parents Alexander Henderson and Jane Robb; siblings Jane, called Jean in the tree and Jane in the 1891 census (about 1862), Janet (about 1865), David (about 1867), Andrew (about 1876): family tree compiled by another researcher and 1871/1881 censuses (index).
  3. Mary Henderson Brown, b. August 18, 1883, 8:20 a.m., Quothquan; registered September 5, 1883, mother informant: Statutory Births, Libberton 650/00 0015, p. 5 (original image).
  4. Agnes McGarth Brown, b. December 18, 1885, 2:30 p.m., Edston, Peebles; registered December 31, 1885, at Peebles by George Brown, father; registrar Geo. Morison: Statutory Births, Peebles 768/00 0149, p. 50, entry 149 (original image). The printed heading added to the digitized image reads "BROWN, AGNES MCGRATH"; the handwritten entry reads McGarth. Both spellings are kept as they appear in their records.
  5. Death of George Brown, April 5, 1886, 1:30 a.m., Edston, aged 23 (original image).
  6. Edston farm cottages: M J Richardson, Geograph 2165948, CC BY-SA 2.0.
  7. Tinto cairn and Quothquan Law: Through Scotland by the Caledonian Railway (1907).

Chapter 3: The Cottages at Quothquan

  1. 1891 Scotland census, Libberton, "Castle," six households, including Jane Henderson, 56, head; Jane, 27; Andrew; James Parker, 18, "Adopted," agricultural laborer, b. Biggar; Mary Brown, 7; Agnes Brown, 5 (Ancestry 1108/4367393, index; original page not seen).
  2. 1881 Scotland census, Libberton 650, ED 3, p. 4, household 18, line 18: James Parker, 8, "Adopted Son," scholar (Ancestry 1119/2528911, index).
  3. Death of Christina Brown, February 10, 1891, Quothquan: Henderson family monument (transcription and photograph); one memorial website gives February 19. The statutory death register, not yet consulted, would settle the day.
  4. Deaths of Jane Henderson, June 8, 1891, and John Archibald, June 20, 1891: Quothquan monumental inscriptions (transcription).

Chapter 4: Shieldhill

  1. Shieldhill House: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB7377 (sixteenth- and seventeenth-century fabric, additions 1820).
  2. Old Quothquan church as Chancellor burial place from about 1780: Wikimedia Commons caption, Quothquan_01.jpg.
  3. Sale of Shieldhill to Nathaniel Dunlop, 1898; rebuilding of Huntfield Place: Quothquan community-council history quoting Tom Brown's account (village history, not a contemporary record).
  4. Shieldhill Hall, 1903, built by Nathaniel Dunlop and Miss E. Dunlop for evening worship: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB12995.
  5. 1901 Scotland census, Libberton 650, ED 3, p. 3, schedules 13–15, roll CSSCT1901_341: Mary Archibald, 35, sewing mistress; James Grossart, 80, road surfaceman, and Marion, 22; Lime Tree Cottage: Andrew Henderson, 25, head; James Parker, 28, boarder, gamekeeper, b. Biggar; Mary Brown, 17, niece, b. Libberton; Agnes Brown, 15, niece, b. Lyne, Peebles (index; original page not seen). Consecutive schedule numbers show the order of the enumerator's route, not which houses shared a wall.
  6. Andrew Henderson as poet and beekeeper: village history quoting Tom Brown.
  7. Dunlop at Govan on census night 1901; Alexander Archibald, domestic gardener at Shieldhill; keepers at Huntfield and Cormiston: 1901 census (index).
  8. James Parker in 1911: gamekeeper, 3 Shieldhill Mains, Libberton, with wife Janet and three children (1911 census, 650/3 ED 3 p. 2, original image).
  9. Agnes Brown's occupation, domestic servant: her son's birth entry, July 4, 1907 (original image). No record found names her employer in 1901–1907.

Chapter 5: Lizzie

  1. Elizabeth Millar McDonald (indexed as Miller), b. May 31, 1874, Liberton, mother Ann, no father named: Scotland, Select Births and Baptisms, Ancestry 60143/7248918 (index; the statutory entry has not been examined).
  2. Marriage of Ann McDonald and Robert Alexander Hope, July 28, 1876, 33 Regent Park Square, Glasgow; emigration to New Zealand, 1878; John Rakaia Hope b. at sea September 26, 1878; Ann d. January 13, 1915, Cross Creek; Robert d. December 3, 1930, Pukekohe: Hope family trees compiled by other researchers (tree 79556812). The details of their emigration come from these family trees.
  3. Robert Hope, b. July 14, 1852, Rigg, Gretna; parents Gavin Hope and Elizabeth Millar: Ancestry 60143/20242563 (index).
  4. 1881 Scotland census, Main Road, Liberton (Gilmerton), ED 7, p. 28, schedule 141: John MacDonald, 52; Janet, 52; Geo, 25; Janet, 15; Alexr, 12; Elizabeth, 6, Grandchild, b. Gilmerton (Ancestry 1119/2158700).
  5. 1891 Scotland census, 14 Wilson Road, Liberton, Newington 685/5, ED 91, p. 11, schedule 49: Elizabeth McDonald, 16, Dom Serv Genl (Ancestry 1108/2264419). The employer's surname is given as indexed.
  6. Marriage of Robert Douglas and Elizabeth Millar McDonald, June 9, 1899, 34 St Patrick Square, Edinburgh, after publication according to the forms of the Free Church of Scotland; officiating minister W. Whyte Smith, B.D., Newington Free Church; witnesses James Finlayson and Janet Page Moodie; registered June 12, 1899: Statutory registers, Marriages, St Giles, 685/4 213 (original image). Robert, 23, saw miller, bachelor, 29 St Leonard's Terrace; father Archibald Douglas, forester; mother Isabella Douglas, M.S. Gray. Elizabeth, 24, domestic servant, spinster, 4 Hatton Place; father John McDonald, coal salesman; mother Janet McDonald, M.S. Page. John and Janet McDonald were her grandparents (1881 census, "Grandchild"); the entry names them as her parents.
  7. Birth of Robert Douglas, May 8, 1876, 3:15 a.m., 9 Canon Street, Edinburgh; father Archibald Douglas, wood merchant's traveller; mother Isabella Douglas, M.S. Gray; parents married January 2, 1863, written as "Liberton"; informant the father; registered May 25, 1876: Statutory registers, Births, St George, Edinburgh, 685/1 845 (original image).
  8. Marriage of Archibald Douglas and Isabella Gray, 1863, Newton, Midlothian, 696/3: Statutory registers, Marriages (index; image not seen). The registration district shows that the "Liberton" on Robert's birth entry is the Midlothian place near Edinburgh, not Libberton in Lanarkshire, the parish of Quothquan and Shieldhill.
  9. 1901 Scotland census, 5 Beaumont Place, Newington, ED 4, p. 5, schedule 24, lines 23–25: Robert Douglas, 24, stone machineman; Lizzie, 26, b. Gilmerton; Janet, 11 months (Ancestry 1101/4385520–1).
  10. Janet Page Douglas, b. April 29, 1900, Robert and Elizabeth Douglas's own daughter: Queen Anne school register; naturalization petition; family knowledge.
  11. Isabella Gray Douglas, infant: family information; no register entry of her birth or death has been found. In the 1911 census Elizabeth gave two children born alive to the marriage, both living; the census does not show which children she counted (Chapter 12).

Chapter 6: The Autumn of 1906

  1. Term days, Whitsunday May 28 and Martinmas November 28 (removal terms fixed by the Removal Terms (Scotland) Act 1886): Scottish National Dictionary.
  2. Women farm servants' wages, southwest Scotland, £7–£10 per half-year with board; scarcity in 1906: Board of Trade, Labour Gazette, 1906.
  3. Weather, August–November 1906: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith station (late-August maxima 76–85°F; gale September 5–6; barometer 29.32 in on September 15; 36°F on September 24; over 1 in of rain in the twenty-four hours ending 8 a.m. October 12; hail, sleet and snow October 13; 38°F on October 14; 52°F on November 28). Leith is about thirty miles from Quothquan; the readings describe the weather there, not in the upper Clyde valley.
  4. Partridge season from September 1, pheasant from October 1: Game Act dates.
  5. Conception window: counted back from a birth on June 14, 1907, assuming a full-term pregnancy.
  6. Father: the father's column in the birth entry of July 4, 1907, is blank (original image). No record seen for this book identifies him.
  7. Illegitimacy rates in nineteenth- and early-twentieth-century rural Scotland: Registrar General for Scotland, annual reports; regional rates were highest in the northeast (Banffshire, Aberdeenshire) and the southwest (Wigtownshire, Dumfriesshire).

Chapter 7: The Road to Edinburgh

  1. Weather, May 28, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (maximum about 52°F, east wind, night minimum 37°F).
  2. Agnes Brown's occupation in 1907, domestic servant, and her domicile, Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar: her son's birth entry, July 4, 1907 (original image). She was living at Gean Cottage. No record shows how she traveled to Edinburgh.
  3. Thankerton station, opened February 15, 1848, goods yard and signal box: Clydesdale's Heritage, "The Station at Thankerton."
  4. Train times and fare: Bradshaw's Railway Guide, May 1900, p. 728 (Carstairs, Symington and Peebles, Caledonian), the nearest timetable consulted; fare calculated at 1d per mile. The 1907 timetable has not been checked.
  5. Stations Carstairs–Princes Street: Caledonian Railway lines to Edinburgh.
  6. Lauriston Place occupants, matrons and telephone number: Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08.
  7. Lauriston Home terms and numbers: Royal Maternity Hospital Annual Report, 1907; A. Nuttall, "Because of poverty brought into hospital," Social History of Medicine 20, no. 2 (2007), 263–280, doi:10.1093/shm/hkm042; Royal Commission on the Poor Laws, report (1909).
  8. Lauriston Home founded 1899 at 118 Lauriston Place: Lothian Health Services Archive, GD1/7.
  9. Edinburgh population, 1901 census about 317,000 and 1911 census about 320,000.

Chapter 8: Born at Nine O'Clock

  1. Royal Maternity Hospital, 79 Lauriston Place: Historic Environment Scotland listing LB44033 (MacGibbon and Ross, 1879; Married Women's Pavilion 1895).
  2. Staff, numbers and practice, 1907: Royal Maternity Hospital Annual Report, 1907; Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08; Nuttall (2007). J. W. Ballantyne's campaign for antenatal care, including the "pre-maternity" bed endowed at the hospital in 1901: Lothian Health Services Archive.
  3. Infant mortality in Scotland, 1907: Registrar General for Scotland, annual report (about 118 deaths under one year per 1,000 births). Infant smallpox vaccination was compulsory in Scotland under the Vaccination (Scotland) Act 1863. Typhoid, cholera, plague and rabies vaccines existed by 1907 but were not given to infants; diphtheria could be treated with antitoxin, but no diphtheria immunization was in general use.
  4. North British Rubber works and McEwan's brewery, Fountainbridge; cable trams, Lauriston Place: Edinburgh directories and Ordnance Survey 1:2500, 1905.
  5. Weather, June 14–15, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (8 a.m. 52°F, calm, cloudy, barometer 29.87 in; 6 p.m. 59°F, wind W force 1, overcast; overnight drizzle; 8 a.m. June 15 57°F, SSE, rain). Edinburgh sunset on June 14 in Greenwich Mean Time, about 9:00 p.m.
  6. Birth, June 14, 1907, 9 p.m., Royal Maternity Hospital: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image).
  7. Zeppelin raid on Edinburgh, April 2–3, 1916, including bombs on Lauriston Place: see Chapter 16.

Chapter 9: His First Name

  1. Weather, July 4, 1907: Met Office Daily Weather Report, Leith (8 a.m. 50°F, ENE force 3, overcast; maximum 56°F, minimum 47°F; 1.4 hours of sunshine; 0.01 in rain).
  2. Registrar's office, 24 Forrest Road; registrar R. D. Robertson: Post Office Edinburgh & Leith Directory, 1907–08; signature on entry.
  3. Entry text: Statutory Births, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, entry 839, p. 280 (original image). The informant's column bears the signature "Agnes Brown, Mother." The entry establishes that Agnes was the informant and signed; it does not show how she came to the office, whether the child was with her, or where either of them went afterward.
  4. Adjacent entries on the same page (original image): no. 838, a girl whose forenames are hard to read (indexed elsewhere as "Philip S.") Campbell Flynn, sex entered as F, born June 17, 1907, 4 a.m., Drummond Street, mother Margaret Flynn, laundress, registered July 3, marked illegitimate, with a marginal note that she was re-registered on June 14, 1956; no. 840, Mary Caldwell Sherra, born June 20, 1907, Royal Maternity Hospital, mother Barbara Bisset Sherra, domestic servant, "domicile — none fixed," registered July 4, marked illegitimate.
  5. Domicile reading: "Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar," read from the magnified original; earlier readings ("Dean," "Brae") are superseded. The 1901 census lists Gean Tree Cottages in the Castle row at Quothquan (schedules 13 and 14, index). The birth entry does not name whom she worked for.
  6. Twenty-one-day limit and section 35 of the Registration (Scotland) Act 1854, with later amendments allowing entry of the father under a court decree: ScotlandsPeople, "Registering illegitimate births"; University of Glasgow, "The Scottish Way of Birth and Death."
  7. Naming for her uncle Lawrence Tweedie Brown: family knowledge, stated by the author.

Chapter 10: Gean Cottage

  1. Agnes Brown's occupation and domicile, "Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar": her son's birth entry, St. Giles, Edinburgh, 1907, no. 839, registered July 4, 1907 (original image).
  2. 1891 census, Libberton ED 3, the "Castle" row (census index transcriptions; original pages not seen): schedule 5, Ann Archibald, 54, crofter, widow, with Mary, 27, Alexander, 20, stonebreaker, John, 17, and a visitor, Isabella Purves, 50; schedule 7, Jane Henderson, 56, crofter, with James Parker, 18, "adopted," Andrew, Jane, 27, dressmaker, Mary Brown, 7, and Agnes Brown, 5.
  3. Mary Archibald, born October 23, 1864, Libberton, daughter of George Archibald and Ann Purves (birth index). Her census ages, 27 in 1891 and 35 in 1901, do not agree with each other; the birth date makes her 26 and 36. John Archibald, born June 16, 1873, died June 20, 1891, and Ann Archibald, née Purves, died December 10, 1897: Archibald family gravestone, Libberton.
  4. Annie P. R. Cuthbertson, daughter of Mary Archibald, died November 22, 1992, aged 94; John Cuthbertson named as "Father": gravestone, Biggar. Annie's birth entry, her surname at birth, and the date of Mary's marriage to John Cuthbertson have not yet been found.

Nathaniel Dunlop was at his house in Govan on census night.

  7. Gean Tree and Lime Tree "were each later converted from two houses into one": Third Statistical Account of Scotland (Lanarkshire), 1960. Gean Tree Cottage, Shieldhill Road, Quothquan: present-day address.
  8. Distance: about 199 feet in a straight line between the present-day map positions of Gean Tree Cottage (55.63941, -3.59841) and Lime Tree Cottage (55.63888, -3.59864), OpenStreetMap via Mapcarta. A parish history page reportedly states that the house still known as Geantree had earlier incorporated Lime Tree Cottage; not independently checked.

Chapter 11: The Gardener and His Sister

  1. 1891 census, Libberton ED 3, the "Castle" row, schedule 5: Ann Archibald, 54, crofter, widow; Mary, 27; Alexander, 20, stonebreaker; John, 17; a visitor, Isabella Purves, 50 (census index transcription; original page not seen).

  4. 1901 census, Libberton ED 3, schedule 3, Shieldhill House: Alexander Archibald, 30, head, domestic gardener; Annie, 26, wife, born Carnwath; Susan Cumisky, 26, dairy maid (census index transcription). Nathaniel Dunlop was at his house in Govan on census night. Jane Henderson's birthplace, Carnwath: 1891 census (Chapter 3).

  6. Agnes Brown's occupation, domestic servant, and her domicile, Gean Cottage, Shieldhill, Biggar: her son's birth entry, St Giles, Edinburgh, 685/04 0839, registered July 4, 1907 (original image). No record found names her employer.

Records that could test this chapter: Lanarkshire valuation rolls, Libberton parish, 1905–06 to 1907–08 (National Records of Scotland, VR series); Royal Maternity Hospital Register of Births, January 1905–July 1912 (LHB3/14/6, Lothian Health Services Archive), which records each mother's last and future place of residence.

Chapter 12: The Douglases

  1. Knighthood of Nathaniel Dunlop, July 15, 1907: London Gazette.
  2. 1911 census, Edinburgh (St Giles registration district 685/4, enumeration district 69, page 11), 16 Lochrin Place, George Square ward, St Cuthbert's parish, April 2, 1911 (original image): Elizabeth Douglas, wife, 36, married 11 years, 2 children born alive, 2 living, born Gilmerton, Midlothian; Janet, daughter, 10, school, born Edinburgh; Laurence B., son, 3, born Edinburgh; Donald Steven (surname hard to read; possibly Stevens), boarder, 25, single, tailor, worker, born Caithness. No head of household is listed. Distance from 16 Lochrin Place to 79 Lauriston Place is about half a mile on today's map.
  3. Isabella Gray Douglas, infant daughter, named for Robert Douglas's mother, Isabella Gray: family information; no register entry found.
  4. Children Act 1908, Part I (infant life protection); registers kept by parish councils and police burghs: Scottish Council on Archives, "Records of child care in Scotland"; Fife Council holds Infant Life Protection Registers of Guardians from 1909.

  6. Surgeon General's report, Smoking and Health, January 11, 1964.

Chapter 32: The Ninth of March

  1. Lung cancer; the family's not knowing of it until he was hospitalized; his sudden admission: recollection of the author's mother. His death certificate, which would give the certified cause, has not been obtained. His smoking, his dress, his love of reading and his nickname "Doug": family recollection.
  2. Death, Thursday, March 9, 1961, St. Joseph's Hospital, Providence, after a brief illness; home 644 River Avenue; age 53; born Edinburgh, Scotland; late parents Robert and Elizabeth (Anderson) Douglas; Bond Clothing Co., own display business, fifteen years for Pawtucket firms; survivors as quoted: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image).
  3. Age at death calculated from the Edinburgh birth entry (June 14, 1907).
  4. St. Joseph's Hospital, 21 Peace Street: dedicated March 20, 1892, and opened in April 1892 as St. Joseph's Hospital for Incurables in the former Harris mansion; cornerstone of a new building laid July 2, 1893; west wing completed October 8, 1930; expansion 1954; Harris mansion razed March 1962: hospital and diocesan histories (secondary).
  5. 56 Dartmouth Avenue and 21 Peace Street lie on the same assessor's plat (44): Providence tax roll.
  6. The Mason Building, 165–169 Weybosset Street (1903); the Outlet Company across the street at 168–176 Weybosset: Downtown Providence historic-district and preservation records. Laurence's workplace at 165 Weybosset: Providence city directories, 1937 and 1938.
  7. Funeral announced for 10 a.m., Monday, March 13, 1961, Ruth E. Urquhart, 812 Greenwich Avenue, Warwick: Pawtucket Times, March 11, 1961, p. 3 (original image). This is an advance announcement; no separate record of the service itself has been seen.
  8. Burial, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5, lot 84: Laurence's own interment record has not been seen. The burial rests on the gravestone, known from a photograph in an Ancestry member gallery (inscriptions: Laurence B. Douglas 1907–1961; Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994), and on the Catholic cemeteries' index, which places Albert Norman Darcy (died October 1, 1954) and Constance Darcy Douglas (1994, grave 3) in section 5, lot 84.

Epilogue: The Names He Carried

  1. Warwick city directory 1963: Constance, widow of Lawrence B., nurse, 119 Phillips Avenue (original image). Warwick city directory 1965: 1292 Post Road, nurse, Briarcliffe Health Center, Johnston (text finding; page image not checked).
  2. Constance Darcy Douglas's practical-nurse training, eight years at Cranston General Hospital, retirement in 1974, residence on Sixth Street, East Greenwich, and St. Francis de Sales Church; death at Rhode Island Hospital; three daughters, twelve grandchildren, two great-grandchildren: her 1994 obituary, seen only as a partial reproduction attached to an online memorial; the original newspaper page has not been seen. Her pleasant nature and the name "Nan": family recollection.
  3. Eugenie E. DeLaire Darcy, 1894–1966, Saint Ann Cemetery, Cranston, section 5: Find a Grave memorial 149385784 (secondary).
  4. Death of Constance Darcy Douglas, April 12, 1994; burial Saint Ann Cemetery, section 5, lot 84, grave 3: Catholic cemeteries' burial index. Stone inscription Constance Darcy Douglas 1912–1994: member-gallery photograph of the gravestone.
  5. Janet Crombie, b. April 29, 1900, d. December 1979, last residence Maywood, Illinois: Social Security Death Index, record 13228117 (index). Duchess of Bedford manifest, arrived September 13, 1929: see Chapter 20. Marriage record giving 1860 South Hamlin Avenue, Chicago: see Chapter 26.
  6. Betty Crombie Mitchell, d. June 23, 2009, Minneapolis: Minnesota Death Index; Star Tribune, June 25, 2009 (index). Jessie Crombie, d. December 12, 2015, Poplar Grove, Illinois: U.S. Obituary Collection, Janesville Gazette, December 15, 2015 (index).
  7. Marriage of Agnes McGarth Brown and Thomas McKenzie, 1911 (original register image). Daughters Mary and Jean: Thomas McKenzie's First World War army service papers (original image). Agnes's portrait: Ancestry member galleries; the provenance description is the sharer's, not independently verified.
  8. Laurence in Pennsylvania from about September 1941: his naturalization witnesses' acquaintance with him from that month (petition 139903, original image) and family knowledge. Where each spouse was on December 7, 1941, is not separately documented.
  9. The pocket watch and the word "Edinburgh" inside its case: in the author's possession.
